lessons.lessonTitle: Rome Wasn't Built in a Day

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: English is an international language. Therefore, it is necessary for
us to learn it. It can be rewarding or just a waste of time. It's up to you. It
depends on how you study it. Here are some tips about learning English.
First, don't be afraid to make mistakes. You will learn from them.
Second, you must not be shy. Be thick-skinned and speak up! Finally,
you must be patient. Remember, "Rome wasn't built in a day."

part3.leadSentence: 本节课主要学习特殊疑问词引导的名词性从句。

blocks.text: 对于特殊疑问句，我们只需要把特殊疑问词后面倒装的句子还原成正常的语序就可以当名词性从句用了，比如：

runs.text: 对于特殊疑问句，我们只需要把特殊疑问词后面倒装的句子还原成正常的语序就可以当名词性从句用了，比如：

blocks.text: What is your name? 变从句 → what your name is. be动词回到主语后面
Where will Vicky go? 变从句 → where Vicky will go. 助动词（can，will，have等）回到主语后面，这类助动词要么本身是情态动词，有确切的意思，修饰谓语动词，要么是为了帮助构成时态，变回陈述句语序后，其意思和时态都不变，因此仍然需要这些词，不能省掉。

reading.text: Listening to music is the favorite pastime of many people all over
the world. This is especially true for people living in Vienna, the city of
song. Being the home of Mozart, this city is the birthplace of classical
music and the waltz.
Music fills the air in Vienna. Going to public concerts is often free
of charge. And don't forget, Vienna is also home to the world famous
Vienna Boys' Choir. No wonder people say Austria is always alive with the sound of music.

part3.leadSentence: 本节课了解be the home of和be home to的用法、掌握动名词短语和不定式短语作主语的区别、了解主语补足语以及No wonder作副词的使用方法。

reading.text: Bungee jumping looks like fun. It makes me nervous just to watch
someone do it. It certainly takes a lot of guts to jump one thousand feet
above the water with only a rope tied to your legs. It scares me just to think about it. However, it is something I really want to do one day.
Some people think I'm crazy. They say to jump is foolish enough,
but to have to pay for it is madness. I don't agree. For me, to live a short
and exciting life is far better than to live a long and boring one. What do you think?

reading.text: Pollution is a big problem in almost all the big cities of the world.
City people are, therefore, becoming more and more worried about how
they can get rid of pollution. They are also concerned about whether the
government is doing enough to protect the environment.
However, people in Ireland don't have these worries. They are sure
that they have found the answer to the problem. They use windmills.
These windmills can create power without creating pollution. This
method is so successful that other countries are thinking of doing the same. Why not? What works for Ireland can work for any other country.

Mr. Chen is talking to his neighbor Mrs. Wang.

runs.text: 从句作介词的宾语如何变化

会直接出现这种表达，会换一种表达方式来解决这个问题，我们来看一个例子：

blocks.text: I am sure of that water is free of charge. 这里的that容易被误认为是water的限定词，而不是名词性从句的连词，因此，在英语中遇到这种情况时，会在of后面加上the fact that, 再加名词性从句，形成"the fact"的同位语从句：

runs.text: that water is free of charge.

blocks.text: 这里面"of the fact"这个介词短语作sure的状语。但这样说实在是啰嗦，所以现代英语里习惯把"of the fact that"这几个词全省了，形成这样的句子：

runs.text: 的状语。但这样说实在是啰嗦，所以现代英语

blocks.text: "That"也可以不省略，但介词一定得省掉，这样剩下的这个名词性从句就代表整个介词短语作sure的状语。我们再举几个例子：

reading.text: Smoking is bad in that it is harmful to one's health. In spite of the
fact that doctors have even warned that it causes cancer, people still keep on smoking.
In some Western countries, however, people are beginning to kick
the bad habit. They realize that health should come first. To help them
quit smoking, there are laws against cigarette advertising and smoking in
public places. This is praiseworthy except that Western countries are
now selling cigarettes in the East in greater numbers than ever. That they are doing this is immoral, don't you think?
Jane is talking to her boyfriend.​

dialogue.text: I'm sorry. I really want to except that every time I get nervous, I can't help smoking.​

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: That's just an excuse.​

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Passing exams is every student's dream. Failing them is their
nightmare. So, to realize their dreams, many students try anything. They
even go to fortunetellers, buy lucky charms and follow old customs.
In Korea, many students bury something personal in the university
they want to enter. They believe that these things will act as magnets and
"pull" them into the university. Whether it works or not, nobody really
knows. At least it does ease the students' minds about passing exams.
Remember, though, you can't always rely on luck. There is no substitute for hard work.
Kim bumps into her classmate, Pak. (K = Kim; P = Pak).

dialogue.speaker: K

reading.text: You are in a strange city. It's late at night and you're tired. But you can't find your hotel. You sigh a deep sigh. It seems like you are dreaming a terrible dream. What is happening?
This situation often happens to people who travel by car. But it may
become a thing of the past. New auto computers are being designed to
tell you how to reach your destination. A small screen in your car
displays a map of the city and shows you where you are. Just give the
computer the name of your hotel. You'll see it on the map. To top it off, a
voice will give you directions while you drive. With a car like this, what else would you expect?
The computer in Dan's car is helping him reach his hotel.

定语从句也叫形容词性从句，因为整个从句是作形容词修饰前面的名词的。我们先来看一下定语从句是怎么来的：

runs.text: 定语从句也叫形容词性从句，因为整个从句是作形容词修饰前面的名词的。我们先来看一下定语从句是怎么来的：

blocks.text: I meet that girl.
That girl has two kids.

如果我们需要用一个形容词来修饰that girl，就非常简单，直接把这个形容词放在girl前面即可。比如用pretty，就直接说that pretty girl。但有时候我们需要用一句话来对that girl进行修饰，就像上面那两句话中"那个有两个孩子的女孩"，就不能直接放在girl的前面，因为"That girl has two kids."这句话不是形容词性的，不能直接用来修饰名词girl，直接这样用会造出这么一个句子：

part3.title: Grammar points
part3.leadSentence: 本课主要学习关系副词引导的定语从句以及suggest的用法。

blocks.text: 关系副词在定语从句中作状语，按照其所作状语的种类可分为时间状语、地点状语、原因状语和方式状语这四类，分别由when、where、why和how引导。关系副词和关系代词可以相互转换：

why = for which

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: When the Japanese ask you, "Would you like some coffee?" think
twice before you answer. In Japan, it is quite popular to have a "coffee
bath." For about US $20, you can get a ground coffee bath; that is, they
"boil" you in coffee. The coffee smells good, but you'll probably feel the heat. It sounds like fun, doesn't it?
Well, the Japanese don't do it for fun. They believe it helps cure
diseases. Who knows? Maybe it's true. But in spite of what they say, I'll just take my coffee in a cup, thank you.
Jack and his Japanese friend, Norie, are on their way home from school. (N = Norie; J = Jack)

part3.title: Grammar points
part3.leadSentence: 本课主要学习不定式短语作help的宾语和宾补可以省略to的用法，并复习名词性从句和感叹句。

blocks.text: 1. 不定式短语作help的宾语和宾补可以省略to
a. help+(to)+动词原形 帮助/忙……
Mother wants me to help (to) do the dishes.

runs.text: Mother wants me to help (to) do the dishes.

blocks.text: 妈妈要我帮忙洗碗盘。
b. help+人+(to)+动词原形 帮某人……

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Would you know what to do during a really big earthquake?
Experts have looked into the matter carefully. It may be worth your
while to look over the following tips they have for us.
If the ground begins shaking while you are driving, pull over and stay in your car. If you are in a building, try to get near a strong wall.
The corner of a room or the space under a big doorway is the safest. As
soon as the quake is over, check the gas pipe in the building. Gas fires
often result from earthquakes. These tips may prove to be lifesavers. We
should, therefore, keep them in mind. Remember to always hope for the best but prepare for the worst.

(Jenny and Andy are having a cup of coffee at a cafe.)
(J = Jenny; A = Andy)

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: Hey, Andy. Did you feel that earthquake yesterday?

/æt wɝk/ /ˈdɪzɪ/
A: Sure. I was at work. Some of the women in the office felt dizzy and
screamed.

/ˈtɛrəˌfaɪd/
J: You know, the ground shook so violently that I was terrified.
A: That sounds just like how a woman would feel.

/brev/
J: I guess we women should be brave like you, huh?
A: Of course! (Jenny shakes the table with her leg.) Aaagh! Earthquake! Help! (He gets under the table.)
J: Look at you—I was just playing. You're worse than a woman. You even sounded worse than the women at the office.

/dʒok/ /skɛr/
A: Uh... I knew it was just a joke. I was only trying to scare you.

/bɛt/
J: Ha! I bet!

疑问词+不定式短语，可以构成名词性短词，此类短语为名词性从句的省略，因此简化的时候需要考虑不定式短语的主语是谁。

what to buy what we should buy what是代词，作buy的宾语

blocks.text: but 在这里是并列连词，表 "除了"，连接两个不定式：

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: When you want to eat at a Western restaurant, you should first
consider making a reservation. If not, you risk having to wait for a long time for a table.
When eating, the Japanese and some Chinese are in the habit of
slurping their food. By doing so, they show their host how much they like
the food. Westerners find eating soup this way most unpleasant. They also
consider picking one's teeth and putting on make-up at the table no-nos.
And when it comes to tipping, they just leave some money on the table.
The amount is up to you, but it's usually 15 to 20 percent of the check.

part3.title: Grammar points
part3.leadSentence: 本课主要学习部分及物动词后必须接动名词作宾语的用法；find作不完全及物动词时，宾语为动名词短语或形式宾语的用法；think/consider/believe这些词也不得直接加不定式短语作宾语，且宾补可以为形容词或名词；并复习条件状语从句。

blocks.text: 1. 部分及物动词后必须接动名词作宾语

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: I remember when I was a young boy, life was tough. My parents
made me do many things for them. For example, they had me do the
laundry, the dishes and the house cleaning. They even got me to work
part-time to help with the family expenses. If I was naughty, they would
spank me. They would not let me go outside the house for days.
Nowadays, life is quite different for kids. Parents can't force them
to do anything. On the contrary, it seems as if children can get their parents to do anything for them. Parents and teachers are even afraid to
spank children for fear of being sued. It amazes me, therefore, whenever
I hear youngsters complain. Instead, they should be thanking their lucky stars.

dialogue.text: Oh... I get it now.

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: One day I was at home listening to music when suddenly I felt a pain
in my neck. As I tried to turn my head, I heard my neck crack. I got the
fright of my life. I was so scared that I could feel my legs trembling. "What's the matter with me?" I thought to myself.
Just then, I felt myself slapped by someone. I opened my eyes and saw my teacher standing over me with an angry look in his face. I
realized then that I had been dreaming. I didn't mind getting caught
dozing off in class. I was happy what happened was just a dream.

part1.dialogueIntro: The teacher wakes me up from my dream. (T = Teacher; M = me)

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Get up, you lazybones!

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: Oh... sorry, sir. I must have fallen asleep.

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: You bet. And we could see you shaking like a leaf.

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: Really? Wow! Thank goodness I was dreaming.

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: What? You were dreaming in class and you are happy about it?

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: Uh... yes, sir.

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: What? Do you take me for a fool?

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: Yes, sir ... I mean no, sir.

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: As punishment you are to write "I must not sleep in class" 100 times.

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: No, sir.

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Wrong. You should say, "Yes, sir."

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: Whatever, sir.

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Oh, I give up.

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: Good, sir.

part3.title: Grammar points
part3.leadSentence: 本课主要复习感官动词作不完全及物动词的用法。

blocks.text: (1) 感官动词是一类用法跟使役动词不一样且具有自身典型特征的不完全及物动词，感官动词对宾语不产生任何干扰，只是宾语做的事情被主语感知到了；而在使役动词形成的句子里，宾语是按照主语的要求去做的，这个结果跟主语紧密相关，相当于主语指使，宾语去做。感官动词可作完全及物动词形成主谓宾，也可以作不完全及物动词形成主谓宾+宾补，比如：

runs.text: 感官动词是一类用法跟使役动词不一样且具有自身典型特征的不完全及物动词，感官动词对宾语不产生任何干扰，只是宾语做的事情被主语感知到了；而在使役动词形成的句子里，宾语是按照主语的要求去做的，这个结果跟主语紧密相关，相当于主语指使，宾语去做。感官动词可作完全及物动词形成主谓宾，也可以作不完全及物动词形成主谓宾

lessons.lessonTitle: Good Feng Shui in New York

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Feng shui, or geomancy in English, is becoming more and more popular in America. The Chinese consider feng shui old news, but to
Americans, it's something brand-new. Store and home owners are
consulting feng shui masters for advice.
How did this ancient Chinese tradition make its way across the seas? The answer is quite simple. Chinese businessmen have been building
high rises in America. They deem it necessary to rely on feng shui
experts, just as they would at home. More and more wealthy Americans are beginning to believe in geomancy. They say that
geomancers in New York make US $250 an hour! In view of this, we
can foresee a bright future for geomancy in America.

part1.dialogueIntro: Ms. Smith, an American, is talking to Mr. Ting, an expert on feng shui. (S = Ms. Smith; T = Mr. Ting)

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: What changes would you suggest for my house?

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: I think that you should get an aquarium with goldfish.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: Why?

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Goldfish bring good luck.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: OK. Anything else?

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: You should also get rid of that mirror in front of your bed.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: Why?

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Your soul travels at night. It must find its way back to the body. The
soul might see your body in the mirror and get confused.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: Hmm... really? What else?

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Um... (He bumps into a coffee table.) Ouch! And get rid of this table.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: Why? It's just a coffee table.

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: It's dangerous. It will bring you bad luck.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: Uh... are you sure?

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: It is a pity that every summer a few people drown at the beach. In
some cases, these people were good swimmers. So how did it happen?
Riptide!
Riptide is a strong underwater current. It moves quickly away from
shore and out to sea. It appears suddenly and pulls its victim under and far off shore. Therefore, people should make it a rule never to swim too far out from the beach.
If you find yourself in a riptide, don't panic. And by no means
should you try to go against the tide and swim back to shore. You'll tire
yourself out and probably drown. Instead, swim parallel to the beach. A
riptide is very narrow. So just a few strokes in the right direction and
you'll be out of danger.

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Some people take the view that sometimes in life we have to take
chances in order to make progress. I admire such people. It certainly takes
courage to take risks. Maybe it's due to my upbringing, but I am the type who likes to play it safe.
People like me believe in the saying, "A bird in the hand is worth
two in the bush." Conservative as it may be, it keeps me out of trouble. I
must confess, however, that such a lifestyle may, at times, be boring.
Admittedly, my life is not half as colorful or exciting as other people's, but at least it gives me a sense of security.

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Fashion never ceases to surprise me. Recently, a fashion designer
came up with another strange creation. His idea comes straight from the
garbage dump, so to speak. He makes sweaters from used plastic bottles.
What a weird sweater that's going to be!
This new kind of sweater will protect you from the rain and cold.
They will, therefore, be especially attractive to outdoor people such as
fishermen, hunters and mountain climbers. However, they're not cheap.
They sell at prices ranging from US $100 to US $150. What a great idea for making money! Don't you think?

part1.dialogueIntro: Andy and Jess are at a fashion designer's party.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: My God, Jess. What's that on Betty's head?

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: Beats me. How weird! I think it's a new kind of hat.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oh, really? If you ask me, it's more like a bird's nest. How stupid it looks!

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: You think so? Hey, wait a minute. You might be right. There's something moving in the nest ... I mean, hat.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Gee whiz! It's a bird.

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: Holy cow! How does she keep it from flying away?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Don't you see? She's got it fastened to a gold chain around her neck.

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: If the bird were strong enough, it could fly her to the moon, so to speak.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That would really be funny.

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: Well, that's fashion!

part3.title: Grammar points
part3.leadSentence: 本课主要学习what引导的感叹句句型并复习反意疑问句的用法。

blocks.text: 1. what引导的感叹句
what引导的感叹句，what是形容词，修饰的核心是名词，结构通常为：

runs.text: 是形容词，修饰的核心是名词，结构通常为：

blocks.text: What + (a/an) +形容词+名词+主语+谓语！
(1) 修饰单数可数名词：What + a/an +形容词+单数名词+主语+谓语!
比如：
It is a beautiful flower. → What a beautiful flower it is!

runs.text: It is a beautiful flower.  → What a beautiful flower it is!

blocks.text: Sharon told an interesting story. → What an interesting story Sharon told!

runs.text: Sharon told an interesting story.  → What an interesting story Sharon told!

blocks.text: (2) 修饰复数名词：What +形容词+复数名词+主语+谓语!
比如：
Anni has big eyes. → What big eyes Anni has!

runs.text: Anni has big eyes.  → What big eyes Anni has!

blocks.text: (3) 修饰不可数名词：What +形容词+不可数名词+主语+谓语!
比如：
There was thick fog this morning. → What thick fog there was this morning!

runs.text: There was thick fog this morning.  → What thick fog there was this morning!

blocks.text: 2. 反意疑问句
反意疑问句是在陈述句后面，附上一个简短的疑问句，用来对前面陈述的内容进行证实、反问、征求对方同意的疑问句，也叫附加疑问句。

runs.text: 反意疑问句是在陈述句后面，附上一个简短的疑问句，用来对前面陈述的内容进行证实、反问、征求对方同意的疑问句，也叫附加疑问句。

blocks.text: 前后主语一致，都用人称代词；前后助动词 /be/ 情态动词一致；前半句有否定词（never/hardly/seldom/little/few/nobody），后半句用肯定。

runs.text: 前后主语一致，都用人称代词

blocks.text: (1) 含 be 动词
结构：be + not + 主语？
You are a student, aren't you?

runs.text: You are a student, aren't you?

blocks.text: He isn't late, is he?
(2) 情态动词（can/will/must/should）
You can swim, can't you?
He won't go, will he?
(3) 实义动词（用 do/does/did）
You like English, don't you?
She likes music, doesn't she?
He went home, didn't he?
(4) 现在完成时 have/has
You have finished, haven't you?

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: When you go abroad, what's the thing you need most? Money, of
course! You'll need to go to the bank to buy some traveler's checks.
Then when you arrive at your destination, you'll have to go to a bank
to cash the checks. Every bank has a foreign exchange department.
However, you'll have to speak with the teller in English because he or she will probably not understand Chinese.
You should, therefore, brush up on some of the words and phrases
that are commonly used when changing money at a bank. For example,
you might want to know what the day's exchange rate is, or if there are
any handling charges, etc. Worried? Don't be. Our next lesson will give you a good idea of what you need to say and how to say it.

part1.dialogueIntro: Richie Li is at a bank in Australia. He tries not to show how nervous he is about speaking English.

dialogue.speaker: R
dialogue.text: Excuse me, miss. I would like to change 500 US dollars into
Australian dollars, please.

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Are you changing cash or traveler's checks?

dialogue.speaker: R
dialogue.text: Traveler's checks.

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Can I have a look at your passport?

dialogue.speaker: R
dialogue.text: Sure. Here you are. By the way, do you charge any commission?

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Not at this bank. Please sign here on your checks. How do you want your money?

dialogue.speaker: R
dialogue.text: Four one-hundred-dollar bills and the rest in smaller bills, please.

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Here you are, sir.

dialogue.speaker: R
dialogue.text: Thanks. You've been very helpful.

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Thank you. Have a nice day.

dialogue.speaker: R
dialogue.text: You too. Goodbye. (Richie says to himself.) Whew! That wasn't so difficult after all.

reading.text: Both my brother and I are outgoing people. He as well as I likes being in the sun. It goes without saying, therefore, that we spend a lot of
our free time at the beach. We go there to relax as well as to keep fit. To be
frank, though, he no less than I enjoys looking at the beautiful "scenery" around the beach.
However, if you are anything like us, we have a piece of advice for
you. Don't forget to rub a good amount of sunscreen lotion all over your
body. Not only does it protect you from getting skin cancer, but it also helps to keep you nicely tanned. Both my brother and I forgot to do that
and now we look like Afro-Americans rather than Chinese.

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Both Charlene and Robert are librarians. Charlene is from America
and Robert is from Australia. Four days after they met face to face for the
first time, they got married. "That was quick," you might think. Actually, they had known each other for nine months before they met. Thanks to
E-mail (electronic mail), they had been corresponding with each other
through their computers.
It all started when Charlene came across Robert's note in her
computer. She replied to it. From then on, they would not only get in
touch but flirt with each other. That was how this "hi-tech" romance
began. Sound interesting? Well, if you're looking for a spouse, why not give it a try? Who knows? You might be just as lucky as Charlene and Robert.

part1.dialogueIntro: Steve is chatting with his sister, Diana.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: Gee, Diana, you're always at home. Don't you have any friends to go out with?

dialogue.speaker: D
dialogue.text: Sure, I do. But all my friends are either out shopping or they're
boring. And you know I hate shopping.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: Get a boyfriend. I'm sure you won't be bored then.

dialogue.speaker: D
dialogue.text: Actually, I want to meet some interesting guys but I don't know how to.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: Why don't you try E-mail? You might get lucky.

dialogue.speaker: D
dialogue.text: I don't think so. Besides, dating through E-mail is neither personal
nor romantic. Why don't you introduce me to some of your friends?

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: Why didn't I think of that? How about my best friend, Fred?

dialogue.speaker: D
dialogue.text: Uh... maybe I'll be better off with E-mail.

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Not only is Thai boxing violent but it is also bloody. Yet it involves the arts of dance and music. It is both ugly and beautiful at the same time. That's why it's so exciting to watch.
Thai boxing was created by soldiers over five hundred years ago. The
fighters use every part of their bodies, especially their feet, knees and
elbows to strike their opponents. Their deadly style has earned them
respect from other martial artists.
Surprisingly, the fights start off with a graceful dance. The dance is in
honor of the boxers' teachers. There is even a small band which plays along with the dance and during the fight. So, who says tough guys don't dance?

part1.dialogueIntro: Martin and Sally have just watched Thai boxing.

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: How did you like the fight, Sally?

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: I found it not only too violent but also very brutal.

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: You're right. It's amazing how the fighters can take not only the
punching but all the kicking as well. I wouldn't be able to handle it.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: Oh, don't be so modest, Martin.

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: No, really. I wouldn't fight one of those tough guys for all the money in the world.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: Would you do it for a kiss?

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: That's a different story. Sure, I will. But you've got to pay in advance. (Martin tries to kiss Sally.)

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: No, please don't. I was only kidding.

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Though it is generally accepted that junk food is not healthful,
American fast-food restaurants are popping up all over the world. These restaurants are for people who are always in a rush. If they don't have
time to sit down to a regular meal, they race over to the nearest
McDonald's. There they can quickly satisfy their hunger.
Because Americans like things done immediately, they often
order their food quickly at fast-food restaurants. They say, "A burger,
fries and a coke!" Though it's not polite, it's efficient. So when you are in the States, try to order this way. After all, in America, do as the Americans do.

part1.dialogueIntro: Tess is a cashier at a fast-food restaurant. Michael is a customer in a hurry. (T = Tess; M = Michael)

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Good afternoon, sir. How are you today?

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: Save it, lady. Just get me a burger and fries.

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Would you care for a drink or anything else?

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: Listen. Though I know you're trying to be nice, I don't have all day.
If I want anything else, I'll mention it, OK?

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Are you sure you don't want a dessert? A milkshake maybe?

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: No, just go and bring me my order, will you?

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Wait a minute! You look familiar. You're Michael Jordan, aren't you?
Tell me, how does it feel to be such a famous basketball player?

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: That's it. I've had enough. I'm going to a real fast-food restaurant.

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Millions of families have trouble falling asleep. Do you know why? There's someone in the family who has a snoring problem. The problem
can be quite serious. In some cases, couples have to sleep in separate
bedrooms. And in others, kids can never study or even watch TV once Dad hits the sack.
So how can we avoid being a snoring nuisance? One way is to avoid
eating a big meal before going to bed. Drinking alcohol near bedtime is
something which also causes snoring. Changing the position in which
the snorer sleeps also helps. Another alternative is to wear ear plugs. But if
all these ideas fail, you have only one choice: Wake the snorer up. Tell
him it's his turn to watch you sleep.

part1.dialogueIntro: A mother and son are talking. (S = son; M = mother)

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: I can't stand Dad's snoring anymore, Mom. I didn't sleep a wink last night.

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: I understand. Neither did I. But what can we do?

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: I read in a magazine that there's some kind of laser which can cure snoring.

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: I read that, too. But it's pretty expensive. Besides, people who
have tried it say it's painful and could cause voice change.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: Oh, I didn't know that. I guess there's no hope then.

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: Well, I'll talk to Dad about it.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: I hope he agrees to do it. Anyway, a voice change will do him a world of good. Have you heard him try to sing lately?

dialogue.speaker: M
dialogue.text: Come to think of it, you're right.

part3.title: Grammar points
part3.leadSentence: 本课主要学习"数以……计的"等短语的用法、关系代词及其修饰的用法，并复习动名词短语作主语的用法和少数不完全及物动词接动名词作宾语的用法。

blocks.text: "数以……计的"等短语的用法
millions of+复数名词 数以百万计的……
hundreds of+复数名词 数以百计的……
thousands of+复数名词 数以千计的……
tens of thousands of+复数名词（系从ten thousand"一万"变化而成） 数以万计的……
hundreds of thousands of +复数名词（系从one hundred thousand"十万"变化而成） 数以十万计的……

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Thanksgiving, which falls on the fourth Thursday of November, is
one of the biggest American holidays. This holiday started in the early
1600's after settlers arrived in America. These people who came from
Europe didn't know how to survive in the wild new country. Luckily, they
met some friendly American Indians, who showed them how to hunt
turkeys and grow corn. In the fall, after the harvest, the settlers had a
great feast. They invited the Indians to thank them for their help.
Today the tradition continues. On Thanksgiving Day, Americans
invite their friends over for a turkey dinner and give thanks for what they have.

part1.dialogueIntro: Larry, who is from Taiwan, is studying in America. His classmate, Sue, who is American, is having a Thanksgiving Day party at her house.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: Hi, Larry. Are you doing anything for Thanksgiving?

dialogue.speaker: L
dialogue.text: I don't have any plans.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: Good. I'm having a get-together at my house. Would you like to come?

dialogue.speaker: L
dialogue.text: Sure, I'd love to. Should I bring anything?

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: No. There will be plenty of salad, ham, corn, potatoes, wine and, of course, turkey.

dialogue.speaker: L
dialogue.text: That sounds great. Do you want me to come by early to give you a hand?

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: That's not necessary. Just come over at around two in the afternoon.

part3.title: Grammar points
part3.leadSentence: 本课主要学习介词与时间的搭配，并复习关系代词的限制性与非限制性修饰、there be句型、使役动词的用法和现在进行时的用法。

blocks.text: 介词与时间的搭配
(1) 表日期或星期几
介词使用 on
例如：on Christmas Day（在圣诞节那天，即 12 月 25 日）、on January 1（在 1 月 1 日）、on Sunday（在星期日）
例如：On Christmas Eve my parents give me a gift.

runs.text: On Christmas Eve my parents give me a gift.

blocks.text: 我父母在圣诞夜时都会送我礼物。

runs.text: 我父母在圣诞夜时都会送我礼物。

blocks.text: Ken is going to play golf on Sunday.

runs.text: Ken is going to play golf on Sunday.

blocks.text: 肯星期日要去打高尔夫球。

runs.text: 肯星期日要去打高尔夫球。

blocks.text: (2) 表年、月、季节、上/下午及晚上
介词使用 in（特例如：at night）
例如：in 1996（在 1996 年）、in July（在 7 月）、in summer（在夏天）、in the morning/afternoon（在早上/下午）
例如：I was born in 1950. 我是 1950 年生的。
Mr. Black sleeps in the morning and works at night.

当先行词为专有名词，比如Beijing、John、家庭成员等能确定具体是某地某人的情况时，无须再对先行词进行限定。此时，后面的定语从句只是对先行词的补充，而非限定，关系代词前须加逗号，翻译时按顺序翻译。比如：

There be句型用来表示某地/某时存在某人/某物，其基本结构是There be + 名词 + 地点/时间状语。注意与表示"拥有"的have进行区分：have表示主语主动拥有某物，There be句型表示客观存在的事物。There be句型属于五大基本句型中最常见的主系表结构。

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Thai people believe that keeping monkeys happy brings good luck.
So every year there's a day on which they have a special treat for
monkeys called the Annual Monkey Feast. Hundreds of monkeys
come from the mountains to "sit at" long buffet tables which are piled
high with bananas, peanuts, watermelons and cabbage.
Monkeys will be monkeys. So they fool around and fights break
out. But nobody seems to care. Neither do the monkeys. They just stare
back at the crowds of people who turn out to watch them. Then they continue to monkey around and have a good time.

part1.dialogueIntro: Paula and Jordan are on vacation in Vietnam.

dialogue.speaker: P
dialogue.text: So where are we going to have dinner this evening, Jordan?

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: Let's go to one of the restaurants by the beach. There are beautiful
sunsets over the bay. And they serve a wide range of exotic food in those restaurants.

dialogue.speaker: P
dialogue.text: That's a great idea. What have you got in mind?

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: I've been dying to try noodles with snails again.

dialogue.speaker: P
dialogue.text: Snails? You've got to be kidding! No way!

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: Come on. You need to be more adventurous. After all.variety is the
spice of life!

dialogue.speaker: P
dialogue.text: Have you eaten noodles with snails before?

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: Sure. It's delicious!

dialogue.speaker: P
dialogue.text: No wonder! Now I know why you're always as slow as a snail!

part3.leadSentence: 本课主要复习简应句的用法，并复习宾语从句和关系代词前置介词的用法以及现在完成时的用法。

blocks.text: 简应句的用法
例：
A: He is stupid.
B: So he is. (=Indeed he is.)
A：他很蠢。
B：他的确很蠢。
A: You can't do it.
B: So I can't. (=Indeed I can't.)
A：你不会做这事。
B：我的确不会。
(1) 否定句用neither （或nor, 使用neither或nor时须采用倒装结构）或either。 neither为副词，故and不可省略，但nor为连词，前面不必置and。
a. be 动词：
主语与be动词倒装。

reading.text: A 34-year-old married man who died recently had no children. When
he died, his wife was not pregnant, either. But now that he's dead, he
has a chance of becoming a father. How's that possible?
After a man dies, his sperm remains alive for some time. In this
case, the woman asked doctors to remove the sperm from her husband's

body and store it in a sperm bank. Now, she can have the baby that she has wanted for a long time. She says it's as if her husband would come back to life again when the child is born. If that is so, wouldn't that make her husband her son?

part1.dialogueIntro: Betty is talking to her husband Dan. (B = Betty; D = Dan)

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Don't you think it's time that we had a baby?

dialogue.speaker: D
dialogue.text: We're much better off without children. Think of all the trouble
raising them.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: But it's only natural that married couples have babies.

dialogue.speaker: D
dialogue.text: I don't want any brats who'll run around the house breaking things.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Then I'll have a baby by myself.

dialogue.speaker: D
dialogue.text: Don't be ridiculous. That's not possible.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, it is. I can adopt or go to the sperm bank or ...

dialogue.speaker: D
dialogue.text: Stop! Are you crazy? I forbid it.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Then, can we have a baby together?

dialogue.speaker: D
dialogue.text: OK. You win.

part3.leadSentence: 本课主要学习now that的用法，并复习定语从句、条件状语从句和虚拟语气。

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: More and more people are forgetting the saying, "Pride comes before
a fall." I remember only a few years ago when things used to be so
different. People used to be more modest and humble.
As I looked around at my schoolmates the other day, I realized how
different things are. People are so much more pretentious nowadays. With
their fancy clothes and stylish hairdos, they appear too materialistic, which
is not to my liking. I know modernization is necessary for advancement.
However, I hope we don't lose our traditional moral values along the way.

dialogue.speaker: K

dialogue.speaker: K

on their arms.

dialogue.speaker: J

reading.text: One of the most convenient but expensive ways to get around a
city in any country is by taxi. And in some cases, tipping is expected.

tour guide. He can take you wherever you want to go. So, however
expensive the taxi ride may be, the advice you get from the driver will
certainly be worth it.

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Today, more people than ever before are speaking to each other
through satellite television, cellular telephones and computers. This means that people from different parts of the world need to be able to
communicate in the same language. That language happens to be English.
Because of this, experts have predicted that more than half of the world's 6,000 languages may die out in the next century. Already almost
all Californian Native American languages are in danger of extinction.
They are being swallowed up by English and other languages.
It is a pity, but that is one of the prices of modernization.

reading.text: Italy is a land of history and culture. And as we all know, the ancient
architecture there is breathtaking. Just as we Chinese are proud of our history and culture, so are the Italians. One of their traditions is to enjoy a

can imagine, after all the eating, drinking and chatting, they need to take a
nap.
Well, this custom may be great for the stomach, but it's not so great
for getting things done. If you happen to be in Italy, don't be surprised if
you have to wait for a long time for the banks and post offices to open.

lessons.lessonTitle: All That Glitters Is Not Gold

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Many people seek fame and wealth. Gul Muhammed sought neither.
However, through fate he is famous. He is so short that he is recorded in the Guinness Book of Records as the shortest man in the world. He
measures only 57 centimeters. Though he has fame, he is not rich.
In fact,he's too poor to pay his own medical bills.
Recently, when Gul became so ill that he had to be brought to the
hospital, he didn't have enough money for the medicine. What a pitiful man he is! His story tells us that fame and wealth do not always go hand
in hand. Indeed, Gul is a living example of the saying, "All that glitters is not gold."

part1.dialogueIntro: Lily is talking to her singer friend, Chad.

dialogue.speaker: L
dialogue.text: Chad, what a lucky guy you are!

dialogue.speaker: C
dialogue.text: What do you mean?

dialogue.speaker: L
dialogue.text: Well, you've got everything a person could ask for: a lovely family, money and fame.

dialogue.speaker: C
dialogue.text: Nothing's as wonderful as it seems.

dialogue.speaker: L
dialogue.text: But such a successful man as you must surely be happy.

dialogue.speaker: C
dialogue.text: Not really. I'm so busy that I don't live a normal life.

dialogue.speaker: L
dialogue.text: Anyway, I wouldn't mind being in your shoes.

dialogue.speaker: C
dialogue.text: And I would love to be able to live as simple a life as you do.

dialogue.speaker: L
dialogue.text: I guess you should never judge a book by its cover.

dialogue.speaker: C
dialogue.text: How right you are!

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Some people say that promises are made to be broken. That certainly
seems to be true in this cutthroat society that we live in. But if you break
your promise, you will ruin your reputation and no one will trust you
anymore. So whenever we say, "I give you my word," we should mean it. There is nothing worse than to be let down by others because they have not kept their promises.
In fact, it isn't so difficult to keep promises. Just remember never to promise anything we are not sure we can live up to. In short, therefore, to
be trustworthy, we should always say what we mean and mean what we say.

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Seeing is believing. But seeing a huge rock half the size of Earth
smash into Jupiter in July 1996 was incredible. Can you imagine what
would happen if Earth collided with a huge space rock? It would be
disastrous. In fact, it is thought that a meteor killed the dinosaurs millions of years ago.
A rock like the one that hit Jupiter could split Earth in two. Doing
nothing about it is like waiting for the end of the world. So scientists plan
to start a project to identify all space rocks that could hit Earth.

part1.dialogueIntro: A student is talking to her teacher.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: I hear that scientists are planning to study asteroids and meteors, right?

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Yes. They want to determine whether Earth is in danger of being
struck by such a rock.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: What if they discover that a big one is coming straight for us?

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: In that case, there are two things they can do. They can launch
rockets to push the rock off its course.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: So that it will miss Earth, right?

dialogue.speaker: T
dialogue.text: Right. And if that fails, we can try destroying the rock with nuclear
missiles.

dialogue.speaker: S
dialogue.text: Wow! I never thought that nuclear weapons could save the world instead of ending it!

lessons.lessonTitle: Don't Be a Fish out of Water

part1.title: Reading&Dialogue

reading.text: Do you sometimes have a hard time understanding what Americans are talking about among themselves? Do you want to know why? The
answer is, Americans are crazy about using slang. They tend to overdo it, though.
Otherwise, slang is fun to use. You should try it. And some slang is easy to understand. For example, if someone is "off the hook," it means

that he is no longer in trouble. The "hook" is a fish hook. If a fish is on the hook, of course, it is in trouble. If it is "off the hook," then it is out of danger. Didn't we tell you slang is fun? Besides, it should at least help you feel more at home and not like a fish out of water when you speak to Americans.

part1.dialogueIntro: Bob, who is Chinese, is speaking to his American classmate, Jill. (J = Jill; B = Bob)

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: Hi, Bob. What's up?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I don't see anything up in the sky. Do you?

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: No, Bob. "What's up?" is slang for "What's happening?"

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Well, why didn't you just ask me that in the first place?

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: Get with it, Bob. Everyone uses slang in America. It makes speech
more colorful.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm having enough trouble learning English.

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: But you should give it your best shot, Bob.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Why?

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: How else can you get to meet American chicks?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: What chicks? I don't like eggs.

dialogue.speaker: J
dialogue.text: "Chicks" mean "girls", you fool.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oh, I give up!
